content:
jordan: kicked off canary shift for release v2.7.3 to 10% in us-west at 14:02. deploy-bot reported healthy start. :rocket:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: release=v2.7.3 stage=canary target=10% initiated_by=jordan
jordan: tagging rollout in release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/2.7.3 -- note: KV cache changes included
ashley: seeing a small uptick in p95 latency on canary nodes, ~120ms -> 220ms. not huge but correlated with increased token lengths in sample set
micah: also seeing 0.6% increase in model-timeouts (client-side), tracing attached: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/canary-traces
paul: quick check: are these canary instances on the new kernel build? (we landed kernel patch in this cut)
jordan: yes, canary is on kernel-5.18.3 + runtime v1.14.2 (same as planned)
ashley: 5xx rate flat so far, but error budget alert is creeping. recommend pausing shift for quick triage. :warning:
micah: +1 to pause. can we pin traffic back to v2.7.2 while we investigate?
paul: if we pin, we should keep the canary pods alive for post-mortem traces. don't drain them immediately.
jordan: pausing now. deploy-bot, pause the shift and pin stable route to v2.7.2
deploy-bot: Traffic shift paused by jordan at 14:06. Current traffic: canary=10%, stable=90%. Pin action: routing.stable -> v2.7.2 (temporary)
ashley: thanks. starting a quick heap/profile capture on canary pods. will paste results in 10m
micah: throwing a limited rollback plan here in case: 1) scale canary down 2) shift back to v2.7.2 3) rollback runtime kernel to 5.17.x on canaries if it reappears
jordan: agreed. but let's wait for profile. if p95 normalizes after pause, we might resume with 5% and extra observability
paul: note to release notes: mark that v2.7.3 contains an experimental KV prefetch; we should flag as opt-in for now
micah: adding a temporary alert tweak to silence noisy p95 flaps for the next 30m so oncall doesn't get spammed
ashley: capture uploaded: s3://redwood-debug/canary/1722222222/profiles.tar.gz
jordan: ok team, keep me posted. if no regressions after 20m we'll do a 5% ramp with stricter canary guards. otherwise we'll cut a rollback and open an incident
micah: FYI I already opened a private doc with initial triage notes: https://docs.redwood/internal/canary-1722222222
paul: pinging infra to standby for a possible quick rollback of kernel bits. @infra-team please ack
deploy-bot: Note: traffic route was pinned to v2.7.2 by jordan. To unpin: use `/deploy unpin routing.stable` or run rollback.
jordan: thanks — will reconvene at 14:30 for stop/go. deciding owners: ashley for metrics, micah for traces, paul for rollout ops
ashley: ack. starting deeper histogram analysis now :mag:
micah: ack. I'll keep trace spans open and correlate request ids with profiles
paul: ack. prepping rollback runbook and release note patch if we need to cut a hotfix
deploy-bot: Reminder: change-window for full rollout is 15:00-17:00 PDT. Any rollback after 15:00 requires oncall+eng-leads approval.
jordan: noted. closing thread for now — we'll post an update at 14:30 with stop/go decision. :white_check_mark:
